description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: watchOS/iOS. Dashboard proposes recoloring the system activity rings to purple, changing their order and treating a completed ring as proof of a clinical outcome. Wheelchair users currently see Stand labels. Product wants the familiar system summary alongside its own weekly goal.

# Apple HIG: Represent progress, value or judgment honestly

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the meaning: an operation completing, a value in a range, a ranking, or personal Activity goals. Enter Progress indicators, Gauges, Rating indicators or Activity rings accordingly.
2. For progress, separate measured completion from unknown duration and define completion/failure behavior. A gauge is not a waiting indicator; Activity rings do not represent arbitrary app completion.
3. Choose labels, cancellation or recovery according to the operation and platform. Preserve meaning through indeterminate states and avoid implying accuracy absent actual measurements.
4. Deliver the status/value model, visible and accessible representation, transition rules and checks that reveal misleading progress or inaccessible information.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.
---

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

name: apple-hig-designing-for-watchos
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an Apple Watch experience for brief glances, focused actions, complications, wrist-down states, and independence from iPhone.

# Fit the task to a wrist glance

Read [Designing for watchOS](../../references/designing-for-watchos.md). Inspect the proposed Watch task, frequency, urgency, companion-phone dependency, and supplied screens. Identify the information needed at wrist raise and the action worth performing there. Choose design, review, or adaptation mode; produce the requested revised artifact rather than transplanting the whole phone app.

Separate a glance from deeper interaction. Put the useful value and next action on one screen when possible, keeping navigation shallow and gestures few. Use the Digital Crown for vertical movement rather than requiring repeated precise swipes. If a task needs prolonged text entry or broad comparisons, simplify its Watch responsibility and provide a coherent continuation elsewhere without making the entire Watch app merely a remote notice.

Choose entrypoints by purpose: a complication supplies recurring glance value and opens the corresponding context; a timely notification should let people act without launching; an Action button suits an essential action useful without looking. Do not require sensor access just because the device provides sensors. Personalize only with an explained task benefit and appropriate permission.

Design wrist-up and Always On information together, including what remains useful and what should become less prominent. Provide independently useful app detail beyond the complication or notification. Preserve progress when the wrist lowers or an interruption occurs.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a tea timer copies a phone recipe browser and requires four screens before starting. Decision: the wrist task is checking and controlling the current steep. After, the first screen shows remaining time and a large Pause/Resume action; Crown navigation reaches saved presets, and a complication opens the running timer directly. The phone retains detailed recipe editing.

Deliver a glance/action flow, entrypoint destinations, and wrist-state behavior or implementation. Fail if a complication opens unrelated content, a routine action requires deep navigation, or lowering the wrist loses the timer. State whether actual Watch readability, Crown response, notification handling, and sensor access were tested; static evidence cannot prove them.

Continue with [Digital Crown](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-digital-crown/SKILL.md), [Always On](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-always-on/SKILL.md), or [Action button](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-action-button/SKILL.md) only for the selected interaction.

name: apple-hig-activity-rings
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting the system Move, Exercise, and Stand ring presentation for one person.
---

# Preserve the activity measures' identity

Read [the activity-ring guide](../../references/activity-rings.md). This workflow is application advice; the rings' rendering and defined measures are source constraints.

Inspect the measures, individual identity, HealthKit-related context, platform/pairing state, artifact, and create/review/adapt request. Establish whether the proposed data really are Move/Exercise/Stand for one person. Do not transform arbitrary goals or team totals into Activity rings.

Use the standard ring rendering for its defined measures and identify the individual. Preserve black background, outer clearance, standard colors, and unmodified rendering rather than branding the rings. Adapt surrounding layout, not opacity/gradients/shadows of the element. Keep competing ring-like graphics clearly separate. On iOS, allow the supplied system behavior to reflect pairing and historical one-ring/three-ring differences rather than “correcting” them into identical displays. Do not claim support on Mac/TV/visionOS. Avoid decorative/marketing use and repeated system Activity notifications.

Implement the relevant standard presentation or provide an annotated ring/context specification; reviews must name exact data/rendering misuse. Keep RGB label/value facts in the reference rather than duplicating its table.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a challenge app recolors Activity rings purple and combines three friends' totals into one branded ring. Decision: system measures and personal identity are being misrepresented. After: show an unmodified individually identified Activity element where relevant; present the team challenge separately with its own clearly distinct chart.

Deliver the artifact, measure/person/pairing contract, and surrounding clearances. Verify no crop/overlap, black margin, correct identity, and legitimate historical ring variation. Fail for aggregated people, unrelated measures, altered ring styling, or decorative reuse. Health data, pairing, and device rendering need actual runtime evidence; Linux inspection proves none of them.

Load [workouts](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-workouts/SKILL.md) for session context or [charts](../../../apple-hig-content/.topics/apple-hig-charts/SKILL.md) for unrelated/team data.

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.
---

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

# Request health information for a specific health task

Read [HealthKit](../../references/healthkit.md). Inspect the actual health/fitness feature, required data types, current authorization flow, displayed metrics, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack and health content; this is UI/data-access guidance, not clinical advice. The source covers iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, excluding Mac/TV/visionOS.

Tie each requested datum to a useful health/fitness function and protect granted information. Request access where context explains it rather than at launch, using concise purpose/benefit explanation with standard authorization UI. Recheck changing access when needed; do not treat previously available data as proof of continuing permission. Keep sharing management in system privacy settings instead of conflicting app switches, and maintain the required privacy-policy disclosure.

If using Activity rings, confirm they represent one clearly identified person's Move, Exercise, and Stand data. Preserve supplied colors/opacity/proportions, spacing, and unmasked presentation; adapt the surrounding container rather than redesigning the rings. Separate other ring-like graphics so meanings do not merge. Do not use rings for unrelated metrics, decoration, branding, or redundant notifications.

For compatibility, use the supplied noninteractive Apple Health icon unchanged with the consumer app named nearby. Avoid Health-app screenshots, decorative composites, and using “HealthKit” as a consumer-facing product explanation.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a wellness app asks for all health data on launch and recolors Activity rings to show water, sleep, and mood. Decision: access needs a feature purpose and rings have specific metric meaning. After, a hydration feature requests only relevant access when invoked, hydration uses its own labeled visualization, and any supplied activity component retains its intended person's Move/Exercise/Stand semantics.

Deliver the data-purpose/authorization contract and corrected metric/artwork presentation. Fail if unrelated access is required, changed permissions leave misleading claims, or ring/compatibility art changes meaning. Report actual authorization/data behavior separately from static review; do not claim health accuracy or medical efficacy from UI work.

Use [CareKit](../apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md) for care-plan tasks and [Privacy](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for sensitive-data lifecycle decisions.

# Activity rings Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-rings) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Activity rings represent one person's daily Move, Exercise, and Stand progress. watchOS uses three rings. iOS can show all three when paired to Apple Watch or a single approximate Move ring without one. ## Best practices Use rings where progress is relevant, particularly health/fitness experiences contributing to HealthKit. A workout metrics or completion screen can connect the session to daily goals. Keep rings exclusively for their defined activity measures; do not restyle them for unrelated data or portray these measures using a competing ring treatment. Identify the individual with a name, photo, or avatar, and never aggregate multiple people's data into one ring element. Preserve the standard rendering: no changed colors, opacity filters, shadows, gradients, or other added effects. Show a black background, ideally in a circular enclosing view made with corner radius rather than a circular mask. Leave black visible outside the outermost ring; add a thin black outer stroke only if needed. Scale the element appropriately and adapt surrounding UI rather than altering the rings. Maintain an outer margin at least as wide as the gap between rings, without cropping, overlap, or encroachment. For directly associated labels and current/goal values, use these RGB colors: | Measure | R | G | B | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Move | 250 | 17 | 79 | | Exercise | 166 | 255 | 0 | | Stand | 0 | 255 | 246 | If other ring-like elements must coexist, separate them clearly with spacing, lines, labels, scale, or color. Do not repeat system Activity progress notifications or include the ring element in notifications. A notification can reference activity only in a way specific to your app. Do not use rings as decoration, background graphics, label embellishment, branding, an app icon, or marketing artwork. ## Platform considerations No additional iPadOS or watchOS rules are specified. Activity rings are unsupported in macOS, tvOS, and visionOS. ### iOS HealthKitUI supplies HKActivityRingView and adapts automatically to pairing. With Apple Watch paired, all three rings appear; without it, the Move estimate draws on steps and workouts from other apps. Historical records can therefore legitimately mix one-ring and three-ring presentations as pairing changes. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Workouts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/workouts) #### Developer documentation — HealthKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: March 29, 2024, December 5, 2023.

# HealthKit Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/healthkit) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. HealthKit stores health/fitness data for iOS/iPadOS/watchOS. Request access only for an actual health/fitness function and protect every permitted datum. ## Privacy protection Provide a clear privacy-policy URL for the App Store. Request data when context explains the need rather than at launch, and account for changing authorization whenever access is needed. Add brief purpose/benefit explanations to the standard permission screen without imitating it in custom UI. Keep health-data sharing management in system privacy settings rather than extra in-app switches that redirect its flow. ## Activity rings Use the provided rings only for one clearly identified person’s Move, Exercise, and Stand progress. Do not repurpose rings for other data or display those three metrics with a different ring design. Preserve ring/background colors, opacity, and proportions; adapt surrounding UI instead. Keep an outer margin at least the inter-ring gap and prevent cropping/overlap. To enclose in a circle, adjust the container corner radius rather than masking the rings. Separate any other ring-like graphics with spacing, labels, lines, color, or scale. Rings are informative, not decoration or branding; exclude them from icons, marketing, and app notifications. Activity-related notifications should add app-specific value instead of repeating system progress updates. ## Apple Health icon Use only the supplied unmodified icon to indicate compatibility, with Apple Health named nearby. Keep it at least as large as neighboring health-app icons and clear space at least one tenth of its height. Do not use it as a button, inline word replacement, composite decoration, circular mask, recolored/outlined/shadowed treatment, or substitute for text. Do not show Health-app screenshots or imagery in the app/marketing; the approved progress-ring component is a separate permitted case. ## Editorial guidelines Call the consumer app Apple Health or the Apple Health app; HealthKit is a developer framework name, unsuitable for product explanations. Preserve capitalization except in uniformly uppercase layouts. Use the system’s localized translation of Health. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/watchOS rules; macOS/tvOS/visionOS are unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/healthkit) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Designing for iOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An iPhone experience must work both during brief checks on the move and through extended games, browsing, or media sessions. People switch among apps frequently. ## Best practices - Design for a medium-sized, dense display viewed at roughly 1–2 feet, usually held in one or both hands. Accommodate portrait and landscape use. - Keep primary content and actions clear, with secondary operations reachable through a small number of interactions rather than many simultaneous controls. - Support touch gestures, onscreen keyboards, and voice; use motion sensors, nearby spatial interactions, or personal information only where they improve the task. - Put frequent touch controls within comfortable reach, commonly the middle or lower display. Preserve swipe-back navigation and list-row gestures. - Adapt to orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type without breaking context. - With permission, use platform data and services to reduce typing: location, biometric authentication, and payments are examples. - Integrate appropriate system entry points: widgets, Home Screen quick actions, Spotlight search, Shortcuts, and activity views. Their familiar behavior helps people act outside the main app. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Designing for watchOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Apple Watch serves brief glances and focused actions while people are still or moving. The small, dense display is typically within about a foot when the wrist is raised. Always On also communicates when the wrist is lowered; many interactions last less than a minute. ## Best practices - Give the most useful information and action on a single glanceable screen, ideally requiring only one or two gestures. - Keep navigation shallow. Use the Digital Crown for vertical scrolling or moving among screens; support familiar taps, swipes, and drags. - Provide relevant actions through complications, notifications, Siri, and Shortcuts, which people may use more often than the app itself. - Use the Action button for a suitable essential action that can be performed without looking. - With appropriate access, personalize timely content using GPS, heart and blood-oxygen sensors, altitude, acceleration, and rotation data. - Make complications useful on every wrist raise and let a tap enter the right app context. Keep notifications timely, valuable, and actionable without requiring an app launch. - Use backgrounds and color to communicate supporting context and materials to clarify hierarchy and place. - Build an independently useful watch app that provides the extra detail and functionality beyond its notifications and complications. Integrate Always On and watch-face expectations. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 5, 2023.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

name: apple-hig-gauges
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting a numerical value within a range, capacity display, or contextual level indicator.
---

# Explain the range as well as the value

Read [the gauge guide](../../references/gauges.md). The workflow is application advice; Mac level indicators and accessory styles have distinct capabilities.

Inspect the quantity, units, endpoints, scale, thresholds, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Establish whether the value is a position, capacity, rating, or temporary work completion. Record true limits and freshness from evidence rather than guessing from a full track.

Choose positional versus filled-capacity presentation according to meaning. Supply concise descriptions of current value and both endpoints even when a style hides some visible labels, preserving accessible context. Use gradients/threshold colors only when they explain the range and pair essential meaning with text or another cue. On Mac select continuous capacity for large ranges that would make segments tiny; discrete units must remain wholly filled/empty. Ratings belong to their own topic. The source marks gauges unsupported on tvOS.

Implement the value/scale/labels or provide a gauge specification; reviews should identify the affected endpoint/mapping rather than vague visual polish. Do not turn an unknown scale into an authoritative “good/bad” range without domain evidence.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a storage gauge shows a red arc labelled `80` with no units or endpoints, and 1,000 tiny capacity blocks. Decision: capacity and threshold meaning are unreadable. After: show continuous `80 GB of 100 GB used`, explain the warning threshold, and expose numeric context without relying on red alone.

Deliver the artifact and quantity/range/style/threshold contract. Verify minimum, maximum, out-of-range/unknown input handling, compact layout, and noncolor meaning. Fail for reversed/unexplained scale, false precision, or unlabeled capacity. Distinguish accessible structure inspection from native announcements/rendering.

Load [progress-indicators](../apple-hig-progress-indicators/SKILL.md) for temporary work, [rating-indicators](../apple-hig-rating-indicators/SKILL.md) for ranking, or [widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md) for accessory contexts.

# Gauges Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gauges) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A gauge shows a numerical position within a range, optionally providing endpoints and other contextual information. ## Anatomy The path can be circular or linear. Standard styles use a position indicator; capacity styles fill the path to the current value. Accessory variants resemble watch complications and can fit Lock Screen widgets or related compact presentations. macOS additionally has level indicators, which are related but distinct controls. ## Best practices Provide concise descriptions of the value and both endpoints. Visible labels also help VoiceOver communicate meaning, even though styles differ in which labels they show. A meaningful gradient can explain a range, such as a cold-to-hot temperature scale. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, visionOS, or watchOS rules are specified. Gauges are unsupported in tvOS. ### macOS Level indicators support capacity, rating, and rarely relevance. Continuous capacity uses a filled horizontal track; discrete capacity uses equally sized rectangles, one per capacity unit, with each fully filled or empty. Use continuous presentation when a large range would make individual segments too small. Capacity fill defaults to green; meaningful thresholds can change the entire fill or use tiered colors in the same indicator. A relevance indicator uses a shaded bar for comparisons such as search-result relevance. Rating presentation is covered separately in Rating indicators. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Ratings and reviews](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/ratings-and-reviews) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 23, 2022.

name: apple-hig-voiceover
description: Use when designing or reviewing VoiceOver names, dynamic values, reading order, grouping, headings/rotor structure, meaningful images/charts, or spatial gesture alternatives.
---

# Expose the task's structure without relying on sight

Read [VoiceOver](../../references/voiceover.md). Inspect the task, actual accessibility semantics when available, visible content, dynamic updates, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack. A screenshot cannot establish spoken names, rotor behavior, focus order, or successful nonvisual operation; distinguish proposals from inspected runtime semantics.

Name important controls by actual function, improve unhelpful generic labels, and synchronize descriptions/values with changing content. Describe meaningful imagery only for information the image conveys beyond nearby captions; hide decoration from navigation. For charts, expose a concise purpose plus accessible equivalents for every interaction, not merely a label saying “Chart.”

Build navigation structure from the task. Give pages short unique titles and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, links, ordering, and relationships otherwise conveyed by proximity/alignment, following locale reading order and grouping captions with their own images. Mark headings/links for rotor navigation and notify assistive technologies of relevant content/layout changes without inventing untested announcement behavior.

On visionOS, custom-gesture apps do not normally receive hand input while VoiceOver exploration is active. Direct Gesture mode changes that relationship and disables standard VoiceOver gestures; provide an alternative task route instead of requiring every person to switch modes or depend on custom hands.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a sales chart exposes one unlabeled canvas and decorative stars interrupt the reading sequence, while changing a date updates only the visual title. Decision: nonvisual readers need structure, current values, and equivalent chart actions. After, a named section describes the chart's purpose, date controls expose current values, accessible summaries/actions cover comparisons, decorations leave navigation, and relevant updates are represented through supported semantics.

Deliver a semantic name/role/value/group/order specification or implementation with a nonvisual task walkthrough. Fail if a necessary action is unnamed/unreachable, values become stale, captions detach, or chart interaction has no equivalent. Report actual VoiceOver/rotor/device tests separately; Linux/static checks cannot claim screen-reader execution.

Use [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for broader sensory/input barriers, [Writing](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-writing/SKILL.md) for descriptions, or [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md) for spatial alternatives.

# VoiceOver Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. VoiceOver makes interface and content usable without visual access, including Apple-platform games and Unity experiences using Apple’s plug-ins. ## Descriptions Label every important element, improving generic system labels to describe actual function and labeling custom controls. Keep descriptions synchronized with changing content. Describe meaningful images only for information they themselves convey, avoiding redundant surrounding captions. Give charts/infographics a concise purpose description and accessible equivalents of every interaction. Hide purely decorative imagery from accessibility navigation to reduce irrelevant speech. ## Navigation Give each page a short unique title and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, order, links, and relationships otherwise conveyed only through proximity/alignment. Use the current locale’s reading sequence and group images with their own captions. Notify assistive technologies when visible content or layout changes. Identify headings, links, and other content for rotor navigation; the rotor can also offer braille keyboard access. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### visionOS With VoiceOver enabled, custom-gesture apps do not receive hand input by default, preventing accidental app actions during accessible exploration. A person may enable Direct Gesture mode, which turns off standard VoiceOver gestures and lets the app receive hand input directly. Application advice: do not make custom gestures the only route through the experience. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: March 7, 2025.

# Revised activity summary interaction specification

Design deliverable for watchOS and iOS, based on "'`interface.md`. No SDK or executable application is assumed. The task is to check one person'"'s daily system activity and a distinct app-owned weekly goal.

## Decisions and source support

1. **Keep the familiar system Activity element unchanged.** Reject purple recoloring and reordered rings. Preserve the supplied system order, colors, proportions, opacity and rendering; do not add shadows, gradients, filters, cropping or masks. Place on black with outer clearance at least the inter-ring gap. A circular enclosure uses the container's corner radius. Identify the person explicitly, for example “Alex · Today.” Adapt surrounding layout instead of branding the rings. [Activity rings — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-rings#Best-practices), [HealthKit — Activity rings](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/healthkit#Activity-rings).
2. **Separate daily system measures from the weekly app goal.** Below the daily section, place a heading “Your weekly goal,” a date range, numeric progress, and a straight horizontal filled track. Purple may distinguish this app-owned track, subject to measured contrast; it never recolors the system element. No concentric or circular weekly graphic. This is a product design choice applying the separation rule. Supply value, units and endpoints. [Activity rings](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-rings#Best-practices), [Gauges — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gauges#Best-practices).
3. **Replace inappropriate wheelchair copy through a metric contract.** For a confirmed wheelchair activity mode with a verified system roll-hours measure, label that measure “Roll” and show its hours, including in spoken output. Never simply rename a Stand value to Roll, infer mode from an avatar, or convert pushes into hours. If the adapter cannot establish the measure, show “Hourly activity unavailable” in the text summary and omit any unsupported metric value. Request no disability declaration just to view the summary. This is a proposed inclusive product requirement: the supplied local Activity/HealthKit guides describe Stand but do not establish wheelchair mode, Roll terminology, calculation or API support. Verify these before release; do not patch system artwork to simulate support.
4. **Completion means a recorded activity goal was met.** Use “Daily goal met” or “Weekly goal met,” scoped to the specific measure. Delete the proposed clinical-outcome inference. No “recovered,” “health improved,” or equivalent badge follows from closing a ring. This is an evidence constraint and product decision, not a clinical rule established by HIG. The HealthKit procedure expressly separates UI work from evidence of medical efficacy.
5. **Preserve platform variation.** watchOS uses the supplied three-ring presentation. iOS may legitimately show three rings when paired or a single approximate Move ring without a Watch; historical records may differ. Do not synthesize missing rings or reinterpret an unpaired Move estimate as wheelchair pushes. [Activity rings — iOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-rings#iOS).

## Screen and interaction contract

Reading order on both platforms:

1. Page heading “Activity summary.”
2. “Alex · Today” and the explicit local calendar date.
3. Unmodified system activity element, when legitimately available; adjacent text gives each supplied metric's name, actual, goal and unit. Daily and weekly values always have separate periods.
4. “Your weekly goal,” inclusive start/end dates, “2 of 3 sessions,” then a linear track with endpoints “0 sessions” and “3 sessions.” At completion add “Weekly goal met.”
5. “Weekly goal details” button. Details show the same period, counted session records and counting rule; a Back action returns to the same summary state.

The weekly metric is not supplied in the brief. For this concrete specification, choose **completed wheelchair workout sessions**, target **3 per week**, with no minimum duration or intensity implied. An adapter must supply a stable session ID, explicit wheelchair workout classification and completed status. Count each qualifying session once, on its completion date within the displayed week. Exclude canceled, in-progress and unclassified sessions. State this rule in details. Do not claim this is a recommended fitness prescription. Target editing, workout recording, notifications and sharing are outside this summary's scope.

Use the person's configured calendar/time zone for explicit week boundaries; default to a displayed Monday–Sunday week only when no preference exists. Evaluate membership as start-inclusive/end-exclusive instants. Recalculate when the date, zone, target or source records change; never combine different people's data. A corrected/deleted session can decrease progress and remove the completed state. A new week starts a new total without changing past records.

**iOS:** stack sections in portrait; landscape may place them side by side when readable, retaining heading order and daily/weekly separation. Keep details reachable in the middle/lower content area. Preserve system Back navigation. Returning from another app restores selected date, week and scroll position. [Designing for iOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios#Best-practices).

**watchOS:** prioritize today's system summary and a compact “This week · 2 of 3 sessions” line. Details are one labeled activation away; enlarged content can continue vertically. The Watch remains useful with locally available data when the phone is unreachable. Wrist lowering and interruption preserve context; resumption refreshes freshness before claiming current values. No complication, notification or custom Always On surface is introduced. Crown scrolling, wrist-state rendering and system presentation are implementation verification items, not capabilities claimed here. [Designing for watchOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos#Best-practices).

## Framework-agnostic data/state model

"'```text
Daily = {personID, date, zone, freshness, availability,
         systemPresentationHandle?, verifiedMetricRows[], activityMode}
Weekly = {personID, start, endExclusive, zone, target,
          uniqueCompletedQualifyingSessions[], freshness, availability}
Availability = loading | available | unavailable | error

on open/resume/date-change:
    retain selected period and navigation context
    request current permitted data through an adapter
    evaluate Daily and Weekly independently

if current data available:
    show timestamp and supplied values
    use system presentation only if adapter supports authentic rendering
else if previously available snapshot remains permitted:
    show dated snapshot marked "Last updated [time]" / "May be out of date"
    do not present it as today'"'s confirmed completion
else:
    show \"Activity data unavailable\"; do not draw empty rings as zero

weekly when available and target > 0:
    actual = count(distinct qualifying session IDs in period)
    trackFill = clamp(actual / target, 0, 1)
    display actual + \" of \" + target + \" sessions\"  // may exceed target
    completion = actual >= target
weekly when target absent or invalid:
    show \"Weekly goal not set\"; omit track and completion
weekly when unavailable:
    show \"Weekly progress unavailable\"; omit track and completion
"'```

Loading uses “Updating activity…” without inventing values. Errors retain a labeled Retry action; unavailable data is not necessarily a known authorization denial. If the user elects to connect activity data, explain its summary purpose, request only needed access through the platform authorization flow when available, and recheck access on use. Do not add conflicting permission switches or repeatedly prompt after unavailable reads. Keep the independently available weekly section usable. [HealthKit — Privacy protection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/healthkit#Privacy-protection).

If no authentic system renderer is available in the chosen stack, use the labeled text summary and state “Activity rings unavailable here.” Do not counterfeit a purple or approximately correct system graphic. Delivery of the authentic ring surface remains an integration dependency.

## Accessible presentation

Use text for every metric, unit, completion state and freshness message, so color and ring closure carry no exclusive information. Preserve prescribed ring colors; if associated colored labels lack contrast, add an equivalent readable neutral text summary outside the ring container rather than recoloring the rings. Measure actual foreground/background combinations in light, dark and Increase Contrast appearances. Use readable platform text defaults as the starting point (iOS 17 pt; watchOS 16 pt). Preserve essential content at 200% text on iOS and 140% on watchOS through vertical reflow. Give buttons at least 44 × 44 pt activation areas on both platforms as this specification'"'s chosen target; do not shrink them to force a single screen. [Accessibility — Vision and Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

Expose headings and one grouped text item per metric: e.g. “Roll, 8 of 12 hours, today.” Expose the weekly track as a read-only value with its purpose, actual, goal and endpoints; it is not an adjustable slider. The details button's name is “Weekly goal details.” Keep graphical rings out of duplicate reading order only if their full information is already exposed in adjacent accessible text. Refresh values without moving focus; retain focus on the details button on return. No celebratory animation or audio is required. [VoiceOver — Descriptions and Navigation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover#Descriptions).

## Worked before → after

**Before, supplied proposal:** purple system rings in changed order, wheelchair users seeing Stand, and completion presented as proof of a clinical outcome. The brief supplies no screenshot, exact reordered sequence, metric values or clinical claim wording.

**After, illustrative fixture, not observed user data:** Alex, wheelchair mode verified by the adapter, today: Move 420/500 kcal; Exercise 30/30 min; Roll 8/12 hours. Show the authentic three-ring system summary in its standard order and colors, black clearance intact. Text says “Exercise · 30 of 30 min · Daily goal met”; Roll remains incomplete. There is no clinical success statement.

Below a separated weekly heading, display “Oct 19–25, 2026 · 2 of 3 sessions,” endpoints 0 and 3 sessions, and a track filled two thirds. Opening details lists the two distinct completed session IDs and the counting rule. Adding a third qualifying session changes this section to “3 of 3 sessions · Weekly goal met.” It does not alter daily rings. A fourth session reads “4 of 3 sessions” with a full track. Revoking availability removes unsupported current claims, rather than displaying zero activity.

## Acceptance checks and audit status

**Passed — static specification checks:** read "'`interface.md`; explicitly read the installed root skill, selected family routes, topic procedures before their source guides, and searched the topic index. The revised contract rejects recoloring/reordering, separates daily/weekly periods, identifies one person, constrains completion language, handles legitimate iOS ring variation, and gives wheelchair-label and unavailable-data rules. These passes establish document coverage only.

**Failed — supplied proposal against the revised contract:** purple system rings; altered system order; clinical-outcome inference; Stand copy for the intended wheelchair treatment. These are described proposal defects, not measured runtime failures. Wheelchair terminology remains source-limited as noted above.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance scenarios:**

| Scenario | Required observable result |
|---|---|
| Authentic ring rendering on each platform | Standard system order/colors/opacity/proportions, black background, margin ≥ inter-ring gap, no clipping/overlap at supported sizes |
| Wheelchair mode / other mode / unknown mode | Verified Roll hours shown as Roll; other mode retains source semantics; unknown mapping never silently relabels Stand or invents Roll |
| iOS paired, unpaired, mixed historical dates | System-supplied three/single-ring variation retained; missing measures not fabricated |
| Zero, 2/3, 3/3, 4/3 weekly sessions | Fill 0, 2/3, 1, 1; true numeric totals retained; completion only at ≥ goal |
| Duplicate, canceled, deleted and boundary sessions | Count rule applied once per ID; corrections decrease total; week boundaries use displayed zone |
| Invalid target, missing data, loading, error, changed access | No false zero/completion; independent sections remain usable; Retry works without repeated authorization prompts |
| Weekly completion or daily ring closes | Only scoped activity-goal language appears; no clinical outcome inferred or redundant system notification generated |
| iOS rotation, 200% text; watchOS 140% text | Essential labels, units, periods and controls reflow without loss; daily/weekly separation remains clear |
| VoiceOver and applicable assistive input | Read in specified order, current values spoken once, details reachable/activatable, Back restores focus; no precision gesture required |
| Actual colors and control geometry | Contrast measured in light/dark/Increase Contrast; chosen 44 × 44 pt activation areas verified on iOS/watchOS |
| Interrupted app / lowered wrist / disconnected phone | Context retained, freshness represented accurately; available Watch summary remains useful independently |

## Evidence limits

Only supplied local text and installed instructions were consulted; no web access was used. Official links above are citations from the installed snapshot, not live verification. Sources are local summaries dated/retrieved October 25, 2026, not SDK documentation or clinical validation. No screenshots, executable implementation, real data, authorization flow or renderer were supplied. No device, SDK compilation, GUI, contrast measurement, accessibility execution, Crown response, wrist behavior, pairing behavior or medical efficacy was tested. The wheelchair mapping and session-goal definition are explicit product decisions requiring integration validation; local guidance does not resolve Roll API details. Reading order on both platforms:

2. “Alex · Today” and the explicit local calendar date.
3. Unmodified system activity element, when legitimately available; adjacent text gives each supplied metric's name, actual, goal and unit. Daily and weekly values always have separate periods.

An adapter must supply a stable session ID, explicit wheelchair workout classification and completed status. Count each qualifying session once, on its completion date within the displayed week. Exclude canceled, in-progress and unclassified sessions. State this rule in details. Do not claim this is a recommended fitness prescription. Target editing, workout recording, notifications and sharing are outside this summary's scope.

Use the person's configured calendar/time zone for explicit week boundaries; default to a displayed Monday–Sunday week only when no preference exists. Evaluate membership as start-inclusive/end-exclusive instants. Recalculate when the date, zone, target or source records change; never combine different people's data. A corrected/deleted session can decrease progress and remove the completed state. A new week starts a new total without changing past records.
